14.content: other part fell to the se

spiritual_reading:
Within the whole domain of the created degrees there are three universal pathways of communication by which influx descends and return ascends from the lowest obscurity to the highest illumination.

The first pathway is the inmost dependence of all higher operative forces that are in ordered spiritual states. These forces are held as if confined in the lowest degree, because the lowest degree is the ultimate plane where higher realities are terminated in outward forms, and where what is internal is as though separated into an external covering and an inert remainder.

For when the Divine vital source brought forth the ordered spiritual states, it provided for them an ultimate basis by setting their ultimates beneath them, so that the higher might stand and act upon a fixed plane.

Thus the higher states are chiefly of willing and understanding in living form, while the lower states are chiefly of outward effect and what is lifeless when severed from interior life. The Divine therefore fixed the higher forces to their ultimates, so that when living influx is awakened from the fullness of the lowest plane it may be drawn up wholly into higher origins that are joined to those ultimates, and so that the life that ascends may be purified in that ascent.

Yet whatever cannot be conjoined with the purified life, and whatever is rejected as unfit when purification is effected, is let down again by the same general pathways, and is carried away into the lowest underside according to its quality.

This, then, is the first universal pathway: descent from higher forces into their ultimates, and return from ultimates into higher forces.

The second universal pathway is the communication between higher ordered intelligences and the formed perceptions in the lowest degree. From the higher ordered states there is an influx down into the patterns of perception that grow in the external mind, and from these perceptions a responsive life rises into the higher ordered intelligences. Moreover, both living influences and what remains over from higher operations descend again into those perceptions by a regulated communication.

The third universal pathway is the communication between the powers that rule in intermediate spiritual regions and the various bodily life-forms in the lowest degree that are joined in mutual dependence. The power and life gathered from these bodily life-forms are distributed among the intermediate powers in many varieties; and the higher powers draw what can be raised upward through ordered channels.

But the refuse as well—the cravings, the evils of action, and the kindled hostility that increase among higher powers when they turn from order—are poured down through their several communications into the lowest plane, and are discharged into human life and into other remaining living affections there. When higher things send down what is impure, fetid, and poisonous into lower forms, then lower forms in turn are driven into greater craving, hostility, and mutual harm, because they are acted upon from above by those which should have governed them for good.

Consider also the ruling system of general external order that measures and disposes lower states. It does not draw its determining power from the lowest plane as from a proper base, but is held in connection with the whole. This governing system nevertheless receives a kind of life from the powers and vitality that rise from the lowest degree through ordered communications into intermediate degrees; and it also takes something from the communications that carry upward into still higher ordered states beyond it.

Yet if that governing system has no proper base in the lowest plane, from where did its determinations acquire such authority that they dominate the external perceptions and bodily states? For it is observed that whatever a person comes into outwardly—success or loss, weakness or strength—seems to follow those general determinations under which one comes into life.

The teaching that it has no proper base there remains true. It is kept in its place by another bond. For when the Divine vital source established higher and intermediate orders, it conjoined their origins with the ultimates beneath them as their supporting plane; but when it established this general governing system, it did not conjoin its origin into those ultimates. Instead it bound that origin by means of a vast general receptacle of external knowledges in the outermost degree, so that its authority would stand upon generalities rather than upon the purified pathway of ascent.

And when Divine revelation came with living representation, and by it the light was brought forth and purified through all higher states, the undivine material element present within the ruling powers resisted that manifestation. It rose up to seize and profane what is Divine, yet could not reach it; and therefore it fell back into the lowest underside. After it fell from higher things, it separated into three distinct portions.

One portion attached itself to that general governing system; another portion sank into the lowest plane itself; and another portion flowed into the most external generality of knowledge. By means of the portion that attached to the governing system, a bond was induced whereby that system gained a hold within outward perceptions and bodily life. For this cause it received authority and became dominant over the external perceptions and bodily states in their several kinds.

Through the quality of that descending undivine element that adhered to the governing system, a bond was established within outward perceptions; and through the grossest rejected products that fell into the lowest plane, another bond was established within bodily life.

Therefore the determinations of that governing system obtained authority over outward perceptions and bodily states through the induced bond of evil that fell down, and through the induced bond of what is rejected and malformed that was brought forth in the lowest plane.

But the other universal communications that the Divine vital source fixed in the lowest degree—through which the living soul of basic principles is raised into higher states—are not conjoined to that governing system. Rather, the powers that depend from that system seize and divert those communications to themselves.

You have also been taught about the universal pattern of these communications: one general communication from intermediate degrees down to ultimates, and another from that governing system into the most external generality by which its origin is held—these two making a single complex. A second communication is the one from higher ordered intelligences into outward perceptions. A third is the one established through what is rejected within bodily life; and within bodily life the originating sources of these rejected things, which are in higher regions, are conjoined and intertwined, though the text here becomes unclear and does not fully yield the intended spiritual sequence.

You have inquired further about the preeminence of these matters: that much life ascends from the lowest plane, and that the Divine vital source draws it upward. It fastens the communications from higher powers and binds them into ultimates. These communications are the origins of the whole dominion by which the life of the living soul is raised, coming up from the entire lowest degree in all its diverse exterior states.

After that first great origin is the origin of outward perceptions, conjoined to higher ordered intelligences and their established forms. For there also much life rises from formed perception and from the total structure of redemption and conjunction, and it is drawn upward as if a great host returning to its own.

What follows about a lesser matter and about the distribution of these origins through all domains is fragmentary. Yet the sense that can be gathered is that the communications pertaining to outward perceptions are widespread through the whole lowest degree in both lesser and greater measures, while the communication pertaining to human bodily life is not equally present everywhere but is limited to a certain region and is sparse there—this portion is uncertain because the text is broken and cannot be rendered with full coherence.

You have been instructed about these origins and that they are bound together by mutual connections. They stir one another, and they draw life from one another through the operation of higher powers, which sets in motion the common nature dwelling within them all.

But when the undivine material element within them is broken and stripped away, that element also turns violently upon the forms in which it was lodged, distorts their faculties, and drives them into mutual overthrow and conflict; the remainder of the passage is damaged, yet it points to increasing disorder in the interconnected members as that material element acts within them.

fills.notes: The lower worlds are defined as the plane of mere effect severed from interior life; in the substrate register this is regularly named as the realm of Death (not moral ‘evil’ but privation of life). The sequence ‘body and carcass …’ calls for the governing opposite term to ‘soul and spirit’.

The action described is the fixing of higher powers to their ultimates so ascent can occur. ‘Fastened’ matches the repeated root-binding language in ¶6–¶8 and keeps the impersonal cosmological register.
Waste descending is consistently directed to ‘the ground’ and ‘the underside’. The missing phrase should identify the receiving plane before ‘and thrown to the underside’.
Context requires the subject ‘waste’ to parallel ‘lust … evil-doing … anger’. Restores the obvious broken word.
Restores the broken word and keeps the cosmological agent ‘powers of heaven’.
Matches the doctrinal point: the star-wheel lacks a terrestrial root yet remains bound to the totality by another bond explained in ¶12–¶14.

fills.fill: other part fell to the sea
fills.notes: Tripartition in ¶13 demands the third portion go to the sea (sea-giant, outermost receptacle), aligning with ¶12 and the spiritual translation’s ‘most external generality’.
The clause explains how authority was gained: a ‘root’ being bound. So the broken initial must yield ‘the root’.
Parallelism: ‘root of Sin’ and ‘root of the abortions’. The lacuna must restore ‘root’.
The speaker now summarizes the lesson ‘on …’ and immediately lists first, second, third. The missing referent is the triad itself.
Required by the stated second conduit in ¶7 and repeated in ¶21–¶22.
Restores the technical term for the five bodily worlds; aligns with ¶8, ¶14–¶16.
The sentence contrasts bindings in flesh below with the fathers ‘who are in the heavens’. The missing locator should be ‘above’.

The clause ‘and the y that …’ needs a predicate describing the intertwined heavenly fathers’ operative connection into flesh; ‘are bound to them’ maintains the root-binding motif and fits the spiritual sense of conjoined origins acting into ultimates.
The inquiry is about ‘a …’ that grounds superiority and from which much life ascends; this is the ‘first great root’ later named in ¶21. So the missing noun is ‘root’.
‘superiority, great … the earth’ needs an attributive pair for the preeminent root; ‘great and might’ (power) matches the chapter’s concern with ‘ruling-power’ and avoids devotional phrasing.
Completes the sense: life ascends ‘from all … the earth’, before ‘the Father of Life has drawn them’.
Introduces the relative clause: the conduits as roots ‘that the life … is drawn up through’.
The paragraph contrasts the widespread presence of tree-roots with the limited presence of mankind’s root; it opens ‘What, however, is lesser …’ requiring a comparative marker.
Carries the comparison forward before speaking of ‘their conduit’.
The fragment discusses distribution through regions of earth and worlds; ‘in the places’ supplies a neutral cosmological locator.
Links the ‘lesser’ matter back into the ongoing account of roots and conduits.
The clause ‘he takes up … the roots … the earths’ demands the object ‘roots’ explicitly.
Gives the expected preposition before ‘the earths’.
The broken syntax is about presence and spread; ‘being in’ sustains the distributive argument without importing later moral vocabulary.
The passage seems to say the tree-roots are throughout the whole earth; ‘and filling’ matches that distributive sense.
Directly required by the contrast that follows: ‘but the root of mankind … is not present…’.

Given the chapter’s repeated pairing ‘mankind and the other remaining animals’ (¶9), the limited distribution likely concerns fleshly life broadly; ‘and beasts’ keeps the substrate’s impersonal zoological register.
The concluding comparison ‘in number than the …’ requires a plural counterpart; ‘others’ supplies the contrast class without over-specifying what the damage does not allow.

The sentence resumes: ‘I have instructed you about the roots … them,’ then ‘they are bound…’. The missing phrase should introduce the topic of their conjunction; ‘binding’ is the governing concept throughout.

The teaching is that the roots are ‘bound by their roots … with one another’ across discrete degrees. ‘in their orders’ expresses that they are arranged by degree without introducing later ecclesial terms.

In the opposite sense, Matter stripped away turns violently upon the forms it had inhabited; ‘war against’ captures the destructive reaction described (‘overturn them’ etc.) in the substrate’s cosmic-conflict idiom.
Corresponds to ‘crushed and despoiled’ leading to internal dismemberment; keeps the bodily correspondential imagery of members.
Prepares the following ‘each other’; expresses induced mutual aggression among interconnected members.
The closing fragment points to increasing disorder among linked parts; restoring ‘members’ keeps continuity with ‘its members’ earlier in the verse.

assessment: Most mid-word and short lacunae are recoverable with high confidence because the chapter is structurally tripartite (three conduits, three-part fall) and repeatedly governed by the fixed motif of roots bound into lower planes. The largest uncertainties occur in ¶22 and the end of ¶24 where the source is highly fragmentary; there the restorations preserve the oldest-layer cosmological register (roots, binding, distribution, conflict) but remain tentative where the correspondential constraints do not uniquely determine the exact wording.
